title: Auto Loans: Payment Crediting, Interest Accrual and Allocation
content:
Every payment received on an Auto Loans account at Piedmont Crescent Bank is credited on a set day and divided among fees, interest and principal under this policy.

## Interest

Interest on Auto Loans is daily simple interest. The interest owing at a given moment is measured on the unpaid principal from the last payment date: the unpaid principal times the annual rate taken as a fraction of one hundred, shared out evenly over the days of the product's interest year, and then times the number of calendar days that runs from the last payment date, not counting that day, up to and including the day of measurement. The figure is carried unrounded until it is used and is then rounded half-up to the cent.

## Crediting day

A payment that arrives on a business day no later than 17:00 Eastern Time counts as credited that day; one arriving afterwards counts as credited on the following business day. Payments can be posted only to a loan that is active or delinquent, as shown by the bank's loan record.

## Allocation of each payment

Each payment is applied following the product's allocation sequence: first to fees due, next to interest accrued through the credit date, and last to principal. The fee share also books a matching fee settlement on the loan, and the credit date becomes the loan's new last payment date. Payments drawn from a PCB checking account are debited from that account.

Stated as a single figure, the principal applied is the higher of zero and the payment amount less the fees due and less the accrued interest.

## Installments

A scheduled installment is satisfied once scheduled payments credited toward its due date add up to at least the monthly payment. The next payment due date then moves forward one month, onto the loan's due day. Because extra payment does not advance the due date, a payment larger than one installment lowers principal but never satisfies a later installment ahead of its time.

## Principal-only payments and prepayment

Where the product accepts principal-only payments and the payment is at least the product's minimum for them, a payment designated to principal only bypasses fees and interest and goes wholly to principal, but only while nothing on the loan is past due; where an installment is past due it is treated as an ordinary scheduled payment. Paying ahead incurs no prepayment penalty, the product's penalty rate being nil.

## Allocation examples (invented amounts)

| Payment | Fees due | Accrued interest | To fees | To interest | To principal |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 500.00 | 25.00 | 120.00 | 25.00 | 120.00 | 355.00 |
| 100.00 | 25.00 | 120.00 | 25.00 | 75.00 | 0.00 |

**Crediting boundary (invented times).** A payment received at 17:00 Eastern Time on a Wednesday that is a business day is credited on that Wednesday; one received at 17:01 is credited on Thursday, provided Thursday is a business day.
